messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert — 3x queue growth on inference-gpu pool (region-us-west). queue_length=~6.2k, gpu_util=99%, autoscaler hit max_nodes. Paging on-call. https://dash.redwood/internal/alerts/1791123581

amanda: oncall here, taking lead. adding @mike and @javi. posting pager handoff in 2.

mike: seeing the same on metrics. autoscaler logs show repeated failures to scale past configured maximum. any recent capacity/param changes?

infra-bot: autoscaler: scale_up_requests=420, active_nodes=60, max_nodes_configured=60, last_scale_err="quota_limit_reached"

javi: quick context — we rolled a continuous-batching change in runtime yesterday (deploy 20260315-2245). batch_window_ms increased from 15 -> 120 for throughput experiments, and prefix_cache.ttl lowered to speed eviction. Could be interacting badly with cold KV cache.

amanda: confirmed deploy 20260315-2245 touched batching defaults. reverting? pros/cons?

mike: immediate question: is autoscaler healthy or legitimately hitting infra quota? If quota, we need handoff to infra/ops for quota bump — otherwise temporary mitigations. Run quick checks: `infractl metrics get pool inference-gpu --fields queue_length,gpu_util,scale_nodes,prefix_cache_hit`

infra-bot: (metrics snapshot) queue_length=6200, gpu_util=99.7, active_nodes=60/60, prefix_cache_hit=0.12

sre-elaine: prefix_cache_hit at 12% is brutal — that will increase per-request work and reduce throughput even if GPUs available. Two parallel mitigations: 1) raise autoscaler max_nodes to buy time; 2) rollback or tune batching to smaller windows so requests flow through rather than waiting for huge batches.

javi: +1. large batch_window=120ms increases head-of-line latency and causes requests to pile up when cache misses are frequent (KV warmup per prefix). Rolling back batch_window to 20ms should restore expected throughput pattern. Also restore prefix_cache.ttl to previous 5m.

amanda: will apply temporary autoscaler bump and then roll back batching. applying autoscaler patch now.

amanda: ```
# temporary increase max nodes to 90
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/pools/inference-gpu/scale-config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"max_nodes":90}'
```

infra-bot: scale-config updated: max_nodes now 90 (requested by amanda). provisioning started, estimate +3m to added nodes becoming healthy.

mike: provisioning visible — nodes_provisioning=18, expected_ready=~180s. ETA OK.

pagerbot: customers impacted: increased 429s and P95 latency spike. top affected tenants: enterprise-alpha, chatflow-inc, docsynth. (see incident dashboard)

customersuccess-raj: I'm pinging the three customers with an interim note. enterprise-alpha seeing message send failures ~15% for last 7 minutes. I'll escalate their CSM.

product-tim: need ETA for recovery + rollback plan. keep updates short for Exec channel.

javi: plan: 1) rollback continuous-batching defaults from deploy 20260315-2245 (batch_window_ms -> 20, max_batch_size -> 8) 2) prefix_cache.ttl -> 300s 3) monitor cache_hit and queue. rollback is config-only, no model restart. executing now.

amanda: running rollback command (redwoodctl):
```bash
redwoodctl config set runtime.continuous_batch.window_ms=20 --pool inference-gpu --author amanda
redwoodctl config set runtime.continuous_batch.max_batch_size=8 --pool inference-gpu --author amanda
redwoodctl config set cache.prefix.ttl_seconds=300 --pool inference-gpu --author amanda
```

infra-bot: config change accepted. rollout id=rb-1791123581-1. Applying to 60 nodes gradually.

infra-bot: prefix_cache_hit increased: 12% -> 38% (1m after config change)

mike: metrics update: queue_length=1200, gpu_util=85, error_rate(5m)=down 70% vs peak. nodes_active=78/90 (autoscaler expansion continuing). P95 latency dropping.

customersuccess-raj: enterprise-alpha reports recovery, they see success rate ~99% now. I'll send status update and close interim ticket if stable for 15m.

product-tim: thanks. roughly how long until autoscaler drains extra nodes? also need rollback PR to protect against accidental future rollouts.

javi: autoscaler will scale down according to normal cooldown (10m) after queue subsides. Action items I propose: (1) add safety that prevents continuous-batching window_ms > 50ms in rolling configs unless opt-in via canary flag, (2) add autoscaler soft limit warning at 80% of max_nodes to alert earlier, (3) postmortem owner + runbook update. I'll own the postmortem.

sre-elaine: adding runbook item: when prefix_cache_hit < 20% and queue_length > 2k, do not increase batch_window beyond 30ms.

amanda: oncall notes: monitoring in progress, will update every 5. tagging @product-tim @customersuccess-raj in exec update. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

pagerbot: alert cleared to SEV2 -> degraded (auto) at 1791125400. Follow-up required: postmortem and infra quota review.

javi: I'll file the postmortem and include timeline, config diff, and recommended guardrails. PR to add canary gating for batching will be in my queue today.

customersuccess-raj: I'll follow up with the three impacted customers with a short RCA note once PM/Ops sign off.

amanda: handing off to oncall-next (mike) for watch. I'm marking incident as mitigated.

mike: ack. continuing watch for 30m, will escalate if metrics regress.

(ends)
_reserved_note: Document represents a Slack incident thread. Messages presented in chronological order, prefixed by sender display names. No title field per agents.md.
